mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC falls below 0.05 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over four consecutive months indicates a contraction in economic output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease of at least 0.1% in the federal funds rate and a monthly increase of at least 2% in the CPI inflation index signals a monetary policy lag, where easing is insufficient to offset inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls > -0.1% AND CPIAUCSL rises > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the trigger occurs but returns are not statistically different from baseline in high inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase of at least 2% in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and a monthly increase of at least 1% in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a robust demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 2% AND HOUST rises > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for five consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for six consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is above 3%.
